title: Understanding Structural vs Managed Risk
text: the only thing you can fully control as an options trader, how much capital you choose to put out. And I have two ways I view it. There's the structural risk, and then there's the managed risk. Structural risk is whatever the cost is for you to put on the thing that you're trading. So, for example, if I'm buying a put and I buy the put for a dollar, my structural risk there is a dollar. If I decide that I have a management point where I'm not actually going to lose the full dollar more likely than not, I am intending to do something before that, that's the managed risk. This can be a little bit difficult because you'll notice that there are some strategies that have defined risk built in, makes it kind of easy, but then there is others that have undefined risk.
